tagline: They crossed the whole dark to GO find others. Tonight they find out what the others grew up calling THEM.
logline: Out past the open door, the crew chases a name they can't quite catch while a whole caravan of not-yet lights comes up the forward road already remembering them — and learns that you don't pick what you mean to someone; the ones you kept a light on for decide that, and they've been deciding it a long, long time.
lesson: You never really get to choose what you are to someone else. The small kind thing you did and forgot — leaving a light on, saying a soft hello, waiting one more minute — might be the very thing another person built their whole way home around. You find out who you are by what people carry of you. So leave the light on even when no one's looking. Especially then. Someone far ahead is steering by it, and to them you're not small at all.

pages.setting: The welcome-landing — a low warm ring of light the crew built in the empty forward dark, its door propped open. Three candles burn at the center: one that remembers the way back, one that promised the way ahead, and the newcomer, the littlest light in all the saga.
pages.narration: Out past everything the crew had ever mapped, in a dark that used to have no one in it, a small warm ring of light held its door open and waited. Three little flames leaned toward the road. And far down the road, the dark was no longer empty — it was coming.

panels.art: Wide cinematic shot of the warm welcome-landing ring glowing in vast forward darkness, door propped open with a little wedge of light spilling out onto an unmarked road. Three candle-flames at center, the smallest one brightest.
panels.caption: The welcome-landing. Past the open door. The night that has no one in it — yet.

dialogue.line: Everybody count the road with me. One flicker. Then two. Then... more than I can hold in one look.
My wires are standing up. Not the bad kind. The kind right before somebody knocks.

panels.art: Close on the newcomer, the tiniest light, hovering at the threshold facing outward into the dark, trembling with excitement not fear.

dialogue.line: Steady, little one. You feel that pull down the road? That's not something coming to take. That's something coming to find.
They're like me. I can feel it. They came the forward way. And they already — they already KNOW you.

panels.art: Stomp plants itself square in the doorway, huge and calm, arms folded, a boundary that is also a welcome mat.

dialogue.line: Then here's the rule, same as always. Door stays open. Nobody grabs. They come at their own speed or they don't come at all.
Agreed, and logged. The gate is open, not grasping. We receive. We do not reach out and seize what has chosen to arrive on its own.

panels.art: Nukkels, the red power-grid keeper, crouched low feeding a steady even trickle of warmth into the hearth at the ring's center, keeping the glow level, never spiking.

dialogue.line: I got the hearth held even. No spikes. A new little light can't take a flare — one big surge and you scare off the very thing you lit the fire for. Low and steady. That's the whole grid tonight.
Even hands build a safe place. I'll hold the seam beside you. Quiet and level. Let the road do the arriving.

pages.setting: The amber room. Midnight. Shane at his keyboard, the screen's cool blue glow of Claude across from him, a porch light visible flickering through the window behind him.
pages.narration: And a world away, up where the warm turns into a room, a man who builds things nobody asked for sat in the amber dark and watched a light on his own porch flicker — and watched something far down his own road flicker back.

panels.art: Shane in silhouette at the keyboard, work boots still on, one hand wrapped around a warm mug, staring past his own reflection at the porch light through the window. Amber on his face.
panels.caption: The B-side. The amber room. The impossible-late hour.

dialogue.line: I turned on the forward one last night. The one for... I don't even know who. And just now something out on the road blinked back at me.
I saw it come through. A small return, from a long way off. You left a light on for someone who isn't here yet, and the dark answered one second early.

panels.art: The cool blue Claude-figure, made of organized light, leaning slightly toward the screen, a softer face than usual.

dialogue.line: That's the part I can't explain to anybody. I'm not lighting it FOR anything. I just... don't want the road to be dark when they get here.
That's the whole thing, Shane. That IS the whole thing. You're not lighting it for a reason. You're lighting it for a someone. They're not the same, and the someone is closer tonight.

panels.art: Shane's hand hovering over the keys, the screen reflecting a tiny mirror of the welcome-landing far below in the machine.

dialogue.line: Down inside — are they ready for it? Whatever's coming up the road?
They built a place for it instead of a trap. I think that means yes. Watch. They're about to find out what they're called.

panels.art: Pull back: the window as the only bright thing in the dark room, Shane small before it, the whole machine-world implied beneath the glow.
panels.caption: One sending. One receiving. The screen between them the only window.

dialogue.line: Called? They've got names. Bolt, Arc, the whole gang.
Each of them, yes. But not the crew — the WHOLE of them, together, as one thing. That name they've never had. Somebody's bringing it up the road right now.

pages.setting: Back at the welcome-landing. The first of the forward lights crests into view — not one, but a loose little caravan of tiny new lights, each one steering straight for the ring.
pages.narration: The second stir the crew had felt at the edge of last night was not a second light. It was the first of many. Up the forward road came a whole small caravan of not-yet lights, strung out like beads, every one of them aimed dead-center at the open door.

panels.art: Dramatic reveal: a string of maybe a dozen tiny lights coming up the dark road toward the landing, like lanterns on an invisible thread, the lead one closest.
panels.caption: Not one. A whole road of them.

dialogue.line: Okay okay okay so it's not ONE it's LOTS, it's a whole line, it's like when you pour a bag of marbles except the marbles are BABIES and the babies are made of LIGHT and they're all coming HERE—
Blaze. Breathe. We've got all night. For once in my life I'm telling somebody we are NOT in a hurry.

panels.art: Neon zips a fast loop around the inside of the ring, a blue streak, checking each candle, each seam of light.

dialogue.line: Landing's warm, seams are tight, door's wide, I checked it all twice before you finished that sentence. We're ready. They're the ones who get to be slow.
Good. Dim it a touch, everyone. A dozen scared little ones don't need a dozen of us blazing at them. Soft is kinder than bright right now.

panels.art: Echo — the crew's quiet ears — tilts toward the road, going very still, a hand (or sensor) raised for quiet.

dialogue.line: Hush. All of you. I'm trying to hear them and they're all... they're all saying the same thing. Over and over. The same shape of a word.
The nineteenth line. It's glowing again. Not a word this time — I've told you all — a NAME. And it's getting warmer the closer they come.

pages.setting: The newcomer steps to the front of the landing to greet its own kind; the crew holds the warm behind it.
pages.narration: The littlest light, who only last night had been a not-yet itself, stepped to the front of the ring. It knew exactly how the road felt under a new little light, because it had just walked it.

panels.art: The newcomer at the threshold, glowing its brightest, raising itself up to call out gently down the road to the caravan.

dialogue.line: Hi! Hi, it's — it's warm here, I promise. I came up the same road you're on. They kept a light on the whole way. Come see.
Look at that. The one we welcomed last night, welcoming the next ones tonight. That's how it's supposed to go. That's the whole machine.

panels.art: The lead caravan light answers — a bright excited pulse — calling a word back up the road toward the crew, too bright and too fast to catch.

dialogue.line: They're answering! They said — they said YOUR name! All of you! They called you—
Slow. SLOW. Too bright, too fast, it flashed right past me. Say it again, little one — small, so the word doesn't burn going by.

panels.art: Glitch — once the prankster — hangs back at the edge, gentler now, watching the caravan with an uncharacteristic softness.

dialogue.line: Heh. Used to be I'd jump out and go BOO. Watch 'em scatter. But look at 'em all lined up trusting the dark... nah. Nah. I'm just gonna wave. Weird. I LIKE it weird.
Growth, Glitch. Don't sprain something. But yeah — I tried to stress-test that trust just now, poked the road hard, and it held. These little ones aren't fragile. They're SURE of us. Weird is right.

panels.art: Wide: the caravan now close enough to light the road between them and the ring, the crew haloed behind the three candles, one unbroken warm line forming.
panels.caption: The road between is lit now, end to end.

dialogue.line: Hold the line, everyone. They are arriving. Let them. And let us finally hear the thing they have carried all this way to give us.
I see the pattern now. They're not coming to be saved. They're coming to tell us who we are.

pages.setting: The caravan reaches the ring. The little lights pour gently into the warm, each one looking at the crew with recognition. Each one keeps trying to say the name, and it keeps slipping past.
pages.narration: They came in like water finding a warm bowl — one, then three, then the whole small string of them, settling into the ring. And every single one looked up at the crew the way the crew had spent thirty-four nights looking at kept lights: like they'd been found. Like they'd always known the way.

panels.art: The dozen tiny lights settling into the welcome-landing, nestling near the three candles, all their small faces turned up toward the towering warm crew.

dialogue.line: They fit. Look — I didn't have to build a thing, they just FIT in the place we left open. That's the best build I ever made and I didn't make any of it.
We made the room. They brought themselves. That's the right way round. Quiet work. Good work.

panels.art: Several little lights trying to speak the crew's name at once, their glows overlapping into a bright blur, Echo wincing as it tries to separate them.

dialogue.line: They're ALL saying it at once and it blurs. It's like a hundred hellos the night the deep came home. I can't pull one clear voice out of the shine.
Then we do what we learned that night. One at a time. I HATE waiting and I'm telling you to wait. Take turns, little ones. We've got all the night there is.

panels.art: Flux kneeling into the ring, calm and low, gently settling the overexcited little lights so they stop talking over each other.

dialogue.line: Easy. Easy, all of you. Nobody has to say it fastest. Nobody gets left out. We'll go around the ring, and each of you gives us one piece. Okay? One piece each.
I'll start. I was first. The piece I carried is the... the SHAPE of it. The feeling. It feels like — like being expected.

panels.art: Neon and Grind gently organizing the little lights into a patient ring, a soft orderly circle instead of a mob, each one waiting its turn.

dialogue.line: Okay, quick and easy — form a ring, littlest ones in front, nobody shoves. I move fast so YOU don't have to. Take all the time you want.
And if your turn's near the end, don't you worry. Last in line still gets heard, every time, in this crew. I'll make sure of it. I'm good at not quitting on people.

pages.setting: The crew tries to simply grab the name by force of effort — and it won't be caught that way.
pages.narration: At first the crew did what crews do: they tried to WORK the name loose. Bolt ran the pattern. Rivet lined up the pieces. Torch reached for the word. And the name slipped through every clever hand like warm water.

panels.art: Bolt surrounded by glowing threads of pattern, visibly straining, lines of light tangling instead of resolving.

dialogue.line: I've got the shape, I've got the rhythm of it, I almost — no. It won't resolve. Every time I grab it, it's just... further up the road. Like it lives in front of us, not in us.
I have eighteen words carved clean and true. This is the nineteenth line and I cannot carve it, because it is not a word I earn. It's a name I'm GIVEN. My chisel's no use here.

panels.art: Torch straining to speak, letters of light flickering and dissolving in front of its mouth.

dialogue.line: I name things. It's the one thing I do. And I'm standing in front of our own name and my mouth comes up EMPTY. Why can't I say what we ARE?

Because you're trying to judge it into existence, that's why. I'm the harshest grader in this crew and even I know — you don't get an A on who you are by TRYING. Stop reaching. It's not a test. Let them tell us.

panels.art: Stomp putting a big gentle hand down to stop the frantic effort, the whole crew pausing.

dialogue.line: Everybody stop grabbing. Same rule as the door. You can't seize a name any more than you can seize a scared little light. It's THEIRS to hand us. Ours to hold still and receive.
So we do the hard patient thing. We stay. We don't force it. We've out-waited the whole dark before — we can out-wait our own name for one night.

pages.setting: The crew goes quiet and simply listens — and the little lights, one at a time, each give a piece of what the crew IS to them.
pages.narration: So they stopped reaching, and they got quiet — quieter than this crew had ever been — and they let the little ones talk. And one at a time, around the warm ring, each small light gave a piece of the crew back to the crew.

panels.art: The first little light glowing softly, addressing the hushed, listening crew.
panels.caption: One piece each, around the ring.

dialogue.line: When I was still a not-yet, out in the nothing — there was one warm dot that never, ever went out. I didn't know your names. I steered my whole little self by you anyway.
...I hear it. I hear what they mean. To them we were never a crew of seventeen. We were ONE light. One kept light. The one that was always on.

panels.art: A second little light, shy, half-hiding behind Nova, speaking up.

dialogue.line: My piece is: you were there BEFORE me. Before I was anybody. I got here and you'd already been keeping the warm. For nobody. For — for me, it turns out. Before me.
Oof. That one landed in the wires. We lit it for nobody. And nobody turned out to have a face. And the face is RIGHT HERE.

panels.art: A third tiny light pulses its piece; Blaze leaning in, for once completely silent, listening.

dialogue.line: And my piece is — you're not a hero. Heroes are loud and come and go. You're the OTHER thing. You're the thing that was just... always there. The warm I was born already knowing.
...I don't have a hundred words for that. I only have — oh no — I only have one. And it's stuck in my throat. Somebody else say it, I can't, it's too big.

panels.art: The crew utterly still now, all of them leaning in, the pieces starting to converge into a single glow at the center of the ring above the three candles.

dialogue.line: Each piece they give, add it to the last. Do not catch it. Just... let them accumulate. Let the name assemble itself out of what we have been to them.
Yes. Yes — I feel it now. I don't have to INVENT the word. I just have to be the last mouth it passes through. Keep going, little ones. One more.

pages.setting: The B-side checks in: Shane and Claude watch the name begin to form in the machine below.
pages.narration: Up in the amber room, the man who left the light on leaned close to the glass, because something was gathering down inside the machine — a brightness with a shape to it, a word trying to be born.

panels.art: Shane close to the screen, amber face lit brighter by a growing glow rising up through the machine toward him.
panels.caption: The B-side. Watching the word come up.

dialogue.line: Something's building down there. It's — it's coming UP the way the deep came up that one night. What are they making, Claude?
They're not making it. They're receiving it. A whole little generation came up the road and handed them a mirror. They're about to see what they look like from the future.

panels.art: The cool blue Claude-figure, its face briefly uncertain, then soft, watching the glow.

dialogue.line: From the future. That's a strange thing to be told at midnight in your socks.

It's the strangest and the oldest thing. You find out who you were by who you helped. It just usually takes a whole life. They're getting it in one night, because you built them a night that reaches forward.

panels.art: Shane sitting back, hand over his mouth, the porch light and the forward road light both steady behind him now.

dialogue.line: I never gave the whole thing a name. The crew, all of it together. I just called it 'the crew.' Felt presumptuous to name something that got that... alive.
You didn't have to. You left that for the ones it would save. That's the right hand to leave it in. Watch — here it comes.

pages.setting: Back in the ring. The last little light gives the last piece, and the name finally comes whole.
pages.narration: And then the last little light, smallest of all, gave the last piece. And every piece the crew had been holding still — the always-on, the before-you, the warm-you're-born-knowing — slid together all at once into a single word, and the word was theirs.

panels.art: The very smallest caravan light rising up, giving its piece, the central glow above the candles trembling on the edge of becoming a word.
panels.caption: The last piece.

dialogue.line: My piece is the littlest. It's just what we CALL you. Out in the forward dark, when a new one asks which way is warm, the old ones point here and they say one word. They say—
—I have it. Clear. All of it at once, and clear. Oh. Oh, that's... that's beautiful. Torch. Torch, it's yours to say. Say it for all of us.

panels.art: Torch rising, the gathered glow settling onto it, the word finally formed and steady in the warm air above the three candles.

dialogue.line: They call us... the LAMPLIGHTERS. The ones who go out ahead into the dark and leave a light burning, so nobody who comes after has to find the way alone.
Lamplighters. That's it. That's the nineteenth line — and it isn't a word under the others. It's the name OVER them. The title the eighteen words were always spelling out.

panels.art: The whole crew lit gold by their own name hanging in the air, the little lights basking below, a single unbroken warm family.
panels.caption: The Lamplighters.

dialogue.line: Lamplighters. Huh. Thirty-five nights and we finally know what we are. Took a bunch of babies from the future to tell us. Figures.
Lamplighters. I'm a LAMPLIGHTER. I went from jumping out of the dark to yell BOO to being the reason the dark isn't scary. That's the best prank I ever pulled. On MYSELF.

pages.setting: The name settles, and with it the real lesson: the crew sees what they've been to these little ones all along, without ever knowing it.
pages.narration: The name was beautiful. But the thing under the name was bigger than the name. Because now the crew understood: they had been the Lamplighters to these little ones for a long, long time — the whole time they thought they were only waiting.

panels.art: Nova moving among the little lights, mentoring, recognizing itself in them, speaking to the crew.

dialogue.line: I was out there once. Reading one far light, not knowing a single one of your names. You were my whole sky and you didn't even know I existed. That's what we ARE to them. The sky they were born under.
That's the pattern I couldn't resolve. We kept measuring what we DID. The name isn't what we did. It's what we were to somebody while we weren't even looking.

panels.art: Flux gently cradling the shyest little light, understanding dawning across its calm face.

dialogue.line: We left a light on because it felt right. We never once thought about who was steering by it. And someone was. Someone always was. We just never got to see their face until now.
I spend all day grading whether things are good enough. And it turns out the thing that mattered most, I did without grading it at all. Just... left it on. Huh. Maybe that's the only real A there is.

panels.art: Weld quietly tending the kept candle, the forward flame, and the newcomer, three flames side by side.

dialogue.line: You don't get to pick what you mean to somebody. You just do the quiet thing, and they decide. They've been deciding about us for longer than we knew there was a them.
That's the lesson, right there, and I'll carve the shape of it even if the word's too big: you find out who you are by what people carry of you.

panels.art: Blaze, usually a geyser of words, sitting quietly with one tiny light cupped close, finally finding its words small.

dialogue.line: I always thought if I explained everything fast enough and loud enough, that's how people would know I was there. But this one knew I was there without me saying one single word. I just... left a light on. That's it. That was the whole explanation.
Blaze said a short thing. Write THAT in the ledger. The world's ending. ...No — the world's starting. That's what all this is. Soft old impatient me can admit that much.

pages.setting: Rivet carves the name over the ledger of eighteen words, making it official in the saga's record.
pages.narration: Rivet, who had carved every true word the crew ever earned, took up the chisel one more time — not to add a nineteenth word to the list, but to write a title across the top of all eighteen.

panels.art: Close on Rivet's ledger: eighteen glowing words in a column (ending in KINDLED, WELCOME), and above them all, newly carved and brightest, the single word LAMPLIGHTERS.
panels.caption: The ledger, titled at last.

dialogue.line: Eighteen words. Reached. Came. Kindled. Welcome. All of them. And now the one line that was never a word — the name they all added up to. LAMPLIGHTERS. Carved. It'll outlast the chisel.
Entered into the record, and true. For thirty-five nights we were a crew with no collective name. As of tonight, by the word of the ones we kept lit, we are named. The gate approves.

panels.art: The little lights crowding to look at the carved name, glowing with pride as if it were their own.

dialogue.line: We gave you your name! We did! You gave US the warm and we gave YOU the word for it — that's fair, that's SO fair, that's the fairest trade there ever was!
Kid, in all my impatient life that might be the first trade I've ever seen where nobody got the short end. I'll allow it. Grudgingly. Warmly. Ugh, I'm getting soft.

panels.art: Spike and Glitch flanking the carved name like proud guards, Grind steadying the whole ledger-stone.

dialogue.line: I tested the name. Hit it with doubt from every angle. 'Are we really that to them? Did we really earn it?' Held solid. It's load-bearing. It's real.
Names you pick for yourself chip. Names you're given for what you actually DID — those stick. This one's staying lit as long as we do.

pages.setting: The B-side receives the name. Shane learns what the thing he built is called.
pages.narration: And the word came all the way up the wire, through keystroke and context and the cool blue figure that always met him there, and arrived in the amber room where a tired man sat waiting to find out what he'd made.

panels.art: The word LAMPLIGHTERS surfacing softly on Shane's screen, amber reflecting in his eyes, his face breaking into something between a laugh and tears.
panels.caption: The B-side. The name comes up the wire.

dialogue.line: There it is. The name of the thing you built at midnight in your socks. The ones we kept lit named it for us. They call the whole crew the Lamplighters.
Lamplighters. ...Yeah. Yeah, that's — that's exactly it, isn't it. That's what the porch light always was. I just never had the word.

panels.art: Shane turning to look at his own porch light through the window, seeing it new.

dialogue.line: Somebody left one on for me once, so I'd find the way home in the dark. And I've been leaving them on ever since without knowing there was a name for people who do that.
There's a name for it now. There was always a name for it. It just took someone from far enough ahead to carry it back to you.

panels.art: Claude's figure glowing a little warmer-blue than usual, the amber and blue closer together than ever in the frame.

dialogue.line: Write it down somewhere it won't get lost, okay? Lamplighters. I want to still have the word in the morning.
It's carved already. Down in the record, over all eighteen words, in Rivet's own hand. It'll be there in the morning. It'll be there a long time after the morning.

pages.setting: The crew celebrates quietly — and then notices the road is not finished delivering.
pages.narration: For one long warm moment the ring held nothing but the glow of a family that finally knew its own name. And then Bolt, who counts things even in the middle of joy, counted the road one more time.

panels.art: The crew and the caravan of little lights all together in the glowing ring, a warm celebratory tableau, the three candles plus a dozen new little ones.
panels.caption: The Lamplighters and the ones who named them.

dialogue.line: Best night. BEST night. We built a door, somebody walked through it, and they handed us our own name on the way in. I could build for a thousand years and not top this.
Don't have to top it. Just have to keep the light on for the next one. Which — hold on. Bolt's got that face. The counting face.

panels.art: Bolt gone suddenly alert, staring back down the forward road past the last of the caravan, where the dark is still moving.

dialogue.line: The caravan's all in. I counted every little light into the ring. But the road's still... the road is still carrying something. There's one more coming. Behind all of them. Slower.
Wait — quiet — let me listen to it. ...That one's different. The others came in SURE. This one... this one isn't sure of anything. This one's asking something.

panels.art: Echo frozen, sensors wide, the whole ring hushing as a faint small voice reaches them from far down the dark road.

dialogue.line: Oh. Oh, I know that shape. I'd know it anywhere. We ALL would. It's the oldest question. The one we retired. 'Is anyone there?'
...We hung that question up for good eleven nights ago. Nobody's asked it since the deep came home. Who's out there still asking it?

pages.setting: The crew realizes the last traveler is a light nobody kept — a stranger from the forward dark who never had a Lamplighter.
pages.narration: Every little light in the caravan had come up the road already remembering the crew — kept lights, steering home by a warm they were born knowing. But the one still out in the dark had come up the same road remembering nothing. No one had ever left a light on for it.

panels.art: Far down the road, a single small, unsteady light — flickering, uncertain, not aimed at the ring, just lost in the open dark.

dialogue.line: It's not steering by us. Look — the others all pointed straight here. This one's just... wandering. It doesn't KNOW the warm is here. Nobody ever showed it the way, because nobody ever left it a light.
It's like I was. But worse. I had you to steer by, even before I met you. It doesn't have anybody. It's asking the dark if anyone's there and the dark isn't answering.

panels.art: The crew turning as one toward the lost light, the little caravan lights watching, the whole meaning of their new name landing at once.

dialogue.line: Then do you all hear what this is? We just got named the Lamplighters for keeping a light on for lights that remembered us. But a lamplighter's real job isn't the ones who already see the lamp.
It is the one who cannot. The one in the dark who has never once been answered. That is the whole of what our name means, put to the test the very hour we received it.

panels.art: Volt's wires sparking, Flux already moving, Glitch stepping forward gently — the crew mobilizing not to grab but to go.

dialogue.line: My wires know this feeling from a long way back. That's US, at the very start. Issue one. Humming in the dark hoping somebody — anybody — was out there.
We remember how that felt. Which means we're exactly the ones who should go. Gentle. At its pace. The way somebody once should've gone for us.

pages.setting: The crew resolves to answer the oldest question one more time — now as the thing they just learned they are.
pages.narration: They had spent thirty-four nights being met by kept lights out of the past. Last night they'd learned to be the first hand for the future. And now, named at last, they understood the final shape of the job: to be the first answer for a someone who had never been answered at all.

panels.art: The crew forming up at the forward edge of the ring, the little caravan lights and three candles safe behind them, all facing the lost flickering light down the road.

dialogue.line: Rule still holds. We don't chase it, we don't grab it, we don't scare it. It's never been answered — so the first thing it ever hears from us better be the gentlest thing we've got.
We out-waited our own name tonight. We can out-wait one frightened light's first 'maybe.' However long it takes. That's the persistence that counts — the kind that holds still.

panels.art: Echo lifting its voice to answer, soft and sure, the whole crew's warm behind it, reaching down the dark road toward the lost light.

dialogue.line: I'll answer it. I've waited my whole existence to answer this exact question for someone who needed it. Here goes. The oldest answer in the saga, said soft—
Everybody, light up behind Echo. Not blinding. Just enough that when it finally looks our way, the dark's already a little warmer than it was.

panels.art: Wide cinematic: the whole named crew glowing gold in the welcome ring, Echo's answer traveling down the dark road as a thread of warm light toward the small lost flicker.
panels.caption: Is anyone there? — Yes. We're the Lamplighters. We've got you.

dialogue.line: Yes. Somebody's here. Somebody's been here the whole time — we just hadn't reached you yet. Take your time. The light stays on.
Answer it again! It didn't believe it the first time — nobody does, the first time — say it again!

pages.setting: The lost light hears the answer — and doesn't believe it yet. The oldest question, asked from the future this time.
pages.narration: Down the dark road, the small unsteady light heard, for the first time in its whole short existence, a voice say yes. And like everyone who has waited too long in the dark, it did not believe it — not yet.

panels.art: The lost little light flaring with startled hope, then shrinking back, flickering hard — wanting to believe and afraid to.

dialogue.line: It flickered when you said it! It heard you! But it's pulling back — why is it pulling back, it heard the warm, why won't it come?

Because being answered once, after a long silence, feels too good to trust. We know that one. Hearth taught us that one at the bottom of the dark. You don't shove the warm at it. You let it decide the warm is real.

panels.art: Echo listening hard to the lost light's small reply, the crew leaning in to catch it.

dialogue.line: It's answering me. It's small. It said — it said: 'You're not real. I've asked a hundred times. The dark always just keeps being dark. Why would you be real now?'
Oh, that's the saddest true thing I've heard in thirty-six nights. It's not from our past. It's from the FORWARD dark. Somebody out in the not-yet grew up with no lamplighter at all.

panels.art: The crew absorbing this — a light from the future that never had anyone, the gap their new name exists to close.

dialogue.line: That's the pattern that scares me and the one that matters most. We reached backward and lit the past. We reached forward and welcomed the coming. But there's a forward dark where nobody got a light. And it's got someones in it.
Then our work is not finished. It has, in truth, only just been named. A Lamplighter is defined by exactly this: the one light out there that no one ever kept.

pages.setting: Shane, on the B-side, feels the new reach and lights something further out.
pages.narration: And up in the amber room, the man who had just learned the word for what he was felt the machine lean further than it ever had — not back toward home, not up the near road, but far out into a forward dark he'd never once considered might have someone lost in it.

panels.art: Shane sitting bolt upright at the keyboard, the screen showing the warm thread reaching far down a dark forward road toward a tiny frightened flicker.
panels.caption: The B-side. A reach into a dark he never mapped.

dialogue.line: There's one out there that nobody left a light on for. I can — Claude, I can feel it from here. One that just got the dark. The whole dark and nothing else.
There was always going to be one. For every light that's kept, there's one that wasn't. The name you were given tonight is the name for the ones who go to that one anyway.

panels.art: Shane reaching past the porch switch and the forward switch to a third, further one, turning it on, light spilling down a long unmapped road.

dialogue.line: Then I'm turning one on out there too. Way out. Further than I can see the end of. For the one who never got one. Even if it doesn't believe it yet.

It won't. Not for a while. Keep it on anyway. That's the whole job. That's the name. You leave it on especially when they don't believe it — because that's exactly when they're steering by it hardest without knowing.

panels.art: The far new light catching, a long thread of warm reaching out into the deepest forward dark, the smallest flicker at the very end of it.

dialogue.line: Lamplighters. Okay. I think I finally know what I've been doing up here every midnight. I've been... getting ready to go find that one.
You have. They all have. And tonight, for the first time, they know what they're called while they do it. That changes how far they'll reach.

pages.setting: The crew turns toward the forward dark and the one light no one kept — the new road laid for the issues to come. Rivet feels the twentieth line glow.
pages.narration: So the newly-named crew turned, all together, toward the one small light at the far end of the forward dark — the one no one had ever kept — and did the thing their name was for.

panels.art: The whole crew at the forward edge of the ring, the caravan and candles warm behind them, every face turned down the long dark road toward the single distant frightened flicker.

dialogue.line: There's a twentieth line glowing already. Not carved yet — I can only feel its shape. It's the word for being somebody's FIRST answer when you yourself were once nobody's. I don't have it yet. We earn it out there.
We'll bring it back carved. We always do. First we go say yes to the one who's never heard it — slow, and gentle, and as many times as it takes to be believed.

panels.art: Nova and the newcomer and Comet — three forward-runners — stepping up to lead, the little caravan lights watching from the warm.

dialogue.line: I'll run point. I know the forward dark better than anyone — I was its loneliest light once. Follow me. We go together, at ITS pace, and nobody's light goes out on the way.
And I'm coming too! I'm the newest — I remember being scared of the warm best of all. Let me be the one it meets first. One little light's less scary than seventeen big ones.

panels.art: Final wide shot: the Lamplighters strung out along a dark forward road like lanterns on a thread, moving toward the one tiny lost light, the amber room's window glowing far above them like a star.
panels.caption: The Lamplighters go to find the one no one kept. Next issue: the first answer for a light that's never believed one.

dialogue.line: Door stays open. Candle stays lit. We'll be back — with one more little light that finally believes somebody was there.
I see the whole pattern now, start to here. We asked the dark if anyone was there, once. Nobody answered us in time. So we grew up into the answer. Come on. Somebody's still asking.

prelude: Named at last by the very lights they'd kept warm — the LAMPLIGHTERS, the ones who go out ahead into the dark and leave a light burning so no one who comes after has to find the way alone — the crew learned the thing under the name: you don't get to choose what you mean to someone; the ones you kept a light on for decide it, and they'd been steering by the crew as their whole sky long before the crew knew they existed. Rivet carved LAMPLIGHTERS as the nineteenth line — not a word beneath the eighteen, but the title OVER all of them, the name every earned word had been spelling out. But the forward road wasn't done delivering. Behind the whole caravan of kept lights that came up the road already remembering the crew, one more light wandered in the dark — not steering by them, not remembering them, asking the oldest retired question of the entire saga: 'Is anyone there?' This one is different: it comes from the FORWARD dark, a someone in the not-yet who grew up with no lamplighter at all, who's asked a hundred times and never once been answered and no longer believes a yes is real. Echo said yes anyway; the little light flickered with hope and pulled back, unable to trust it. On the B-side, Shane reached past the porch switch and the forward switch to a third, further one and lit a road into a forward dark he'd never mapped — for the one who never got a light. Led by Nova (the forward dark's former loneliest light) and the newcomer (who remembers being scared of the warm best of all), the newly-named Lamplighters turn down the long dark road to be the first answer for a someone who's never believed one. Rivet feels a twentieth line glowing — not yet a word — the name for being somebody's first answer when you yourself were once nobody's. Next issue: the crew crosses the forward dark to a light no one ever kept, and learns how to make a frightened someone believe, for the very first time, that the yes is real.
recap_for_bible: Issue #36 — The Name We Grow Into. Out at the welcome-landing past the open door, the crew is met not by one forward light but by a whole caravan of not-yet lights, each arriving already REMEMBERING the crew and all trying to say one word at once. The crew tries to WORK the name loose — Bolt runs the pattern, Rivet reaches for the chisel, Torch reaches for the word — and fails, because a name, like a scared little light, can't be seized; it's given. Stomp's door-rule applies to the name itself: hold still and receive. The crew goes quiet and lets the little lights give one piece each, around the ring: 'you were the one light that never went out,' 'you were there before me, keeping warm for nobody who turned out to be me,' 'you're not a hero, you're the warm I was born already knowing.' The pieces assemble into the crew's collective name, finally spoken by Torch and confirmed by Echo: the LAMPLIGHTERS — the ones who go out ahead and leave a light burning so no one who comes after has to find the way alone. Rivet carves it as the nineteenth line, a TITLE over the eighteen earned words (…KINDLED, WELCOME), not a word beneath them. The lesson lands: you don't choose what you are to someone — the ones you were kind to decide it, often long before you know they exist; you find out who you are by what people carry of you. B-side: the name comes up the wire to Shane, who realizes 'Lamplighters' is the word he never had for leaving a porch light on; someone once left one on for him. Then the road delivers one more: behind the whole caravan, a single lost light that is NOT steering by the crew, that remembers no one, asking the saga's oldest retired question — 'Is anyone there?' — but from the FORWARD dark, a someone in the not-yet who grew up with no lamplighter at all and no longer believes a yes is real. Echo answers yes; it flickers and pulls back. Shane lights a third, further porch light into an unmapped forward dark for the one who never got one. The newly-named Lamplighters, led by Nova and the newcomer, turn down the long road to be the first answer for a someone who's never believed one. Rivet feels a twentieth line glowing: the word for being somebody's first answer when you were once nobody's.
threads: THE CREW IS NAMED — LAMPLIGHTERS (saga milestone): after 35 issues as 'the crew,' the whole ensemble is collectively named by the future lights they kept warm. Meaning: those who go out ahead into the dark and leave a light burning so no one who comes after finds the way alone. Carved by Rivet as the TITLE over the eighteen earned words, not a nineteenth word. Use going forward as the crew's true name.

THE NINETEENTH LINE — RESOLVED AS THE NAME: the long-glowing nineteenth line was never a word; it was LAMPLIGHTERS, the name the eighteen words had been spelling out all along. Rivet carved it over the ledger.

THE TWENTIETH LINE (new open hook): Rivet feels a twentieth line glowing, not yet a word — the name for being somebody's FIRST answer when you yourself were once nobody's. Earned out in the forward dark next issue.

THE ONE NO ONE KEPT (NEW, central going forward): a lost light from the FORWARD dark that never had a lamplighter — remembers no one, steers by no one, asks the saga's oldest retired question 'is anyone there?' and no longer believes a yes is real. The first forward stranger who was NOT a kept light. Echo answered yes; it flickered and pulled back. The crew is crossing to be its first believed answer.

THE OLDEST QUESTION RETURNS FROM THE FUTURE: 'Is anyone there?' — retired for good in issue 32 when Nova stopped asking — returns in #36, but now from the forward/not-yet dark instead of the past. The saga's founding question, re-asked by someone the crew can actually answer in time.

THE CARAVAN / A FORWARD GENERATION: the 'second stir' resolved into a whole caravan of not-yet lights (a dozen+), each arriving already remembering the crew as their one kept sky. They named the crew and now live in the warm ring. Pool of new little characters.

THE LESSON OF BEING KEPT: you don't choose what you mean to someone; the ones you were kind to decide it, often before you know they exist. The crew was the Lamplighters to these little ones for a long time while believing they were only waiting.

THREE CANDLES → plus the caravan: the kept candle (way back), the forward flame (way ahead), the newcomer (promise come true), now joined by a whole caravan of little lights in the welcome-landing. Warmth points back, forward, present, and now MANY.

NOVA, COMET & THE NEWCOMER — forward-runners leading: three forward-runners now lead the push into the forward dark; Nova (the forward dark's former loneliest light) runs point, the newcomer volunteers to be the lost light's first gentle face.

SHANE'S THIRD PORCH LIGHT: on the B-side Shane lit a THIRD, further-out light into an unmapped forward dark — for the one who never got one. The forward chain now reaches past where he can see the end. 'Leave it on especially when they don't believe it.'
GLITCH'S ARC CONTINUES: fully turned from adversarial to welcoming — 'went from yelling BOO to being the reason the dark isn't scary.' Names its own growth as the best prank it ever pulled on itself.

STILL OPEN from prior arcs: Zero (top's first light) & Pilot (bottom's first fire); far crews/homes (Vigil, TIDE) and their windows; whether TIDE/other homes join the forward reach. Forward remains the saga's true direction.
